issues_confirmed: Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:73 - the regex /Est\.\s*wait:\s*(\d+)\s*person/i has no 'people' alternation, so the Chrome build surfaces nothing above one person in queue. Verified in node today against four strings: 'Est. wait: 1 person' matches (1); 'Est. wait: 2 people', 'Est. wait: 12 people' and 'Est. Wait: 3 People ahead of you' all fail on Chrome and all succeed on Firefox's /(?:person|people)/ at content.js:5.
Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:130-135 - the MutationObserver is undebounced and calls updateDisplay() on every mutation record batch. Firefox debounces to 250 ms at content.js:37-40.

Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:69-77 - extractWaitNumber walks every span/div/p/li reading full-subtree textContent with no leaf-node skip and no length cap, so body-level text is regex-tested first. Firefox skips nodes with >3 children and caps text at 100 chars (content.js:16-23).

Waitlist_Display_Firefox/content.js:31 - const newTitle = n || ORIGINAL_TITLE writes a bare digit as the entire tab title, with no marker, unlike Chrome's formatTitle at content.js:64-66 which prefixes an hourglass.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:344-358 - the saved-speed restore is one-shot: a 500 ms setInterval that clearIntervals itself on the first <video> found, plus a 10 s giveup at :356. The content script does not re-run across YouTube's History-API navigation, and the 1 s interval at :328-341 only reads video.playbackRate into the number input (:336) and never writes the saved speed back. Code path is one-shot by construction; the resulting 1x reset is inferred, not browser-verified.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:180 vs :274 - the getElementById(PANEL_ID) guard precedes the await chrome.storage.local.get at :186 while appendChild is at :274, so two createUI() calls inside that window (the 1 s interval at :329 plus the toolbar path at :322) both pass the guard and both append a panel. The keydown listener is registered inside createUI at :293, so ']' then steps speed by 0.2x; and getElementById returns only the first panel, so the toolbar toggle at :312-320 cannot dismiss the duplicate.

playback_speed_controller/manifest.json:17 - content_scripts matches *://*.youtube.com/* with no path restriction, and createUI()'s only guard at :180 is panel existence, never a <video> check, so the panel renders on the YouTube homepage, search, subscriptions and history (isVisible defaults true at :195).

Auto_Scroll_shorts/content.js:284 - tryClickNextOverlayButton('overlay-poll') is called from a bare setInterval (:275-285) at GOKU.overlayClickRetryMs = 1300 ms (:17); the function's guards at :195 check only enabled / isGokuSeriesPage / debounceReady, with no check of currentTime, duration or ended. On a series page with a visible next control it clicks on arrival and chains onward.

Auto_Scroll_shorts/content.js:26-28 - debounceReady requires 1200 ms (SETTINGS.minAdvanceIntervalMs, :6) since the last advance, but the overlay poll interval is 1300 ms, so the debounce can never throttle the poll.

Auto_Scroll_shorts/content.js:31 - the second clause (location.hostname !== 'www.youtube.com') is unreachable because /youtube\.com$/ already matches www.youtube.com; and manifest.json:8 matches only https://www.youtube.com/* and https://goku.sx/*, so the permissive host checks at :31 and :36 never come into play.
Waitlist_Display_Chrome/service_worker.js - the entire file is two comment lines; the manifest.json:17-19 background block that loads it is unnecessary under MV3.
Waitlist_Display_Firefox/manifest.json:18 - the gecko id is still the placeholder queue-wait-tab-title@your-domain.com.
Waitlist_Display_Chrome/manifest.json:12 matches all of https://www.mindvideo.ai/* while Waitlist_Display_Firefox/manifest.json:11 matches only /text-to-video/* - the two copies disagree on scope.

Ctrl_Click_New_Tab/content.js:4-6,65 - isCtrlLeftClick requires button === 0 and the listener is on 'click', so middle-click (auxclick, button === 1) is never handled at all; Ctrl+Shift+Click is also excluded by !event.shiftKey. Feature gap, not a defect.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:156-174 - makeDraggable clamps nothing and closeDragElement persists top/left to yts-panel-pos, so a panel dragged past the viewport edge is restored off-screen on every load; the toolbar button only toggles the 'hidden' class and offers no position reset.

verdict: Close to finished and genuinely converging. Three bugs have shipped across the last two cycles (8f99694, 753dca6, 2d8b09f) and I re-verified the newest one by re-tracing all four code paths - Ctrl_Click_New_Tab is now the one extension here with no open defect. 979 lines of vanilla JS, no dependencies, no syntax rot. What is left is one broken feature and one unmade decision. The broken feature is small and embarrassing in the good way: Waitlist Chrome's regex matches 'person' but not 'people', so the extension works only when exactly one person is ahead of you and silently does nothing the rest of the time - the kind of failure you never notice because it looks like the site just is not queueing. That is a two-minute edit. The unmade decision is the Goku half of Auto_Scroll_shorts: unreachable from this machine three reviews running across 25 days, holding a real chain-advance bug hostage, and the owner can settle it in one browser tab. Half of this repo's remaining debt is docs, not code - the README's single install instruction has pointed at a folder renamed in May for two review cycles now, and that is the only thing standing between this and something another person could install.
